newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sugar imports seen at 180,000t in '96/97.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sugar imports seen at 180,000t in '96/97.

text.p: Singapore's raw sugar imports in 1996/97 (June/July) will probably remain steady near last year's 180,000 tonnes, industry officials and traders said on Monday.

About 60-70 percent of the total, or about 110,000-130,000 tonnes, will be bought from Australia, while the remaining 30-40 percent will come mainly from Thailand, South Africa or Fiji, an official familiar with Singapore's raw sugar imports said.

"The choice of sourcing that sugar will depend on the kind of premiums origin-sellers offer," the official said. "About 60-70 percent will likely be sourced from Australia and the rest from other countries."

Raw sugar sales by Australia to Singapore declined in 1995/96 to 80,000 tonnes from 166,000 tonnes in the previous year largely because of increased competition from Thailand and South Africa, Queensland Sugar Corp chief executive David Rutledge said in an interview with Reuters on Monday.
"Singapore importers have had a long-standing relationship with Australia and their imports should easily come back," one trader said.
But the Singapore industry official said the reason Australian imports had declined was due to the supplier opting to sell in other markets.
Singapore sugar importers will not be buying any material from Cuba because of concerns over quality, dealers said.
Traders said a prime alternate source for sugar importers in the city-state would be Thailand.
"In the first half of 1997, the new Thai crop will become available while the Australians will not come in until the second half of the year," one trader with a Western commodity house said.
